translation.text: And from there I went to another place of the earth[a], and he showed me a mountain of fire that blazed day and night.

footnotes.text: The subject of 'he showed me' is implicit in the Ge'ez; context suggests Enoch's angelic guide.

source.text: ወሖርኩ፡ መንገሌሁ፡ ወ*ነጸርኩ፡ ሰብዐተ፡ አድባረ፡ ክቡራነ፡ ወኵሉ፡ ፩እምነ፡ ፩እንዘ፡ ይትዌለጥ፡ ወእእባኒ፡ *ክቡራነ፡ ወሠናያነ፡ ወኵሉ፡ ክቡር፡ ወስቡሕ፡ ራእዮሙ፡ ወሠናይ፡ ገጾሙ፡ ፫መንገለ፡ ጽባሕ፡ ወ*ጽኑዓን፡ ፩ዲበ፡ ፩ወ፫መንገለ፡ ሰሜን፡ ፩ዲበ፡ ፩ወቈላት፡ ዕሙቅ፡ ወጠዋያት፡ *አሐቲ፡ ለአሐቲ፡ ኢይትቃረባ።

translation.text: And I went in that direction and saw seven glorious mountains[a], each one differing from the other; and their stones were glorious and beautiful, and all of them were glorious and splendid in appearance, and fair in face. Three were toward the east, one set upon another, and three toward the north, one set upon another, with deep and winding ravines[d][c][b], no one coming near to another.

footnotes.text: The Ge'ez description of the final landscape features is difficult. The clause rendered 'with deep ravines and one valley' may describe the spaces between the mountain groupings rather than an additional feature beside them.
The phrase 'fair in face' is intentionally retained from the Ge'ez imagery, which describes the mountains in almost personified visual terms.
Or 'with deep ravines and one valley, and they did not come near one another.'.

source.text: ወሳብዕ፡ ደብር፡ ማእከሎሙ፡ ለእሎንቱ፡ ወ*ኖኆሙ፡ ዘይትማሰሉ፡ [ኵሎሙ፡] ከመ፡ መንበረ፡ አትራኖስ፡ ወ*የአውድዎ፡ ዕጸወ፡ መዓዛ።

translation.text: And the seventh mountain was in the midst of these[a], and its height surpassed them all, resembling the seat of a throne[c][b], and fragrant trees encircled it.

footnotes.text: The word rendered 'in height' comes from an uncertain OCR reading; the sense is that the mountain's elevation or lofty form resembled a throne-seat.
The phrase 'seat of a throne' preserves the Ge'ez double expression rather than simplifying it to merely 'throne.'
Or 'among them, and in height it resembled'.

translation.text: And among them was a tree whose fragrance I had never smelled[a][b].

footnotes.text: The middle phrase is textually difficult in this OCR witness. It likely describes the tree's scent or aromatic quality as exceptional, with the comparison pointing to myrrh or a similar fragrant resin.

source.text: ውእተ፡ ጊዜ፡ እቤ፡ ዝንቱ፡ ሠናይ፡ ዕፀ፡ ወ†*ሠናይ፡ ለርእይ፡† ወአዳም፡ ቈጽሉ፡ ወ†ፍሬሁኒ፡† ሞገስ፡ ጥቀ፡ ለርእዩ፡ ገጽ።

translation.text: Then I said, “This is a beautiful tree, beautiful to look upon[a]; its foliage and fruit were exceedingly pleasing in appearance[b].”

source.text: ውእተ፡ ጊዜ፡ አውሥአኒ፡ ሚካኤል፡ ፩እምፄ፡ መላእክት፡ ቅዱሳን፡ ወክቡራን፡ እንዘ፡ ምስሌየ፡ ሀሎ፡ ውእቱ፡ ዘዲቤሆሙ።
